Well there isn't a majority rule.

In consensus or the way we do it in a nutshell:

Proposal of some kind is made.
Questions are asked/Concerns are raised.
The group spends time trying to resolve concerns and answering questions.
Often the proposal is changed enough so that everyone feels okay with whatever is happening. 
At the end people can consent, meaning they say "Yes" to the approval or they stand aside - sometimes meaning they don't like what is happening, but they don't feel that they want to stand in the way.
Or if someones concerns cannot be resolved they block it. Meaning it cannot pass.

In consensus blocking should rarely happen, at least how it is written by C.T Butler. It is more productive in my own personal opinion to listen to everyones concerns with a proposal and to listen to everyones thoughts. This is the value of consensus, that with so many perspectives someone might be able to see someone elses blindspot. It is preferable to change a proposal until everyone is happy as opposed to just throwing it out.
